lessons.title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
lessons.notes_html:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) is the ability of a computer or machine to perform tasks that typically require human intelligence. These tasks include understanding language, recognizing images, solving problems and making decisions.

Where AI Is Used

  • Healthcare, finance and education — AI improves efficiency, accuracy and decision-making.
  • Transportation and entertainment also use AI in daily life.

Machine Learning (ML)

Machine Learning is a branch of AI that enables computers to learn from data and improve their performance on tasks without being explicitly programmed. Instead of following fixed instructions, ML algorithms analyze patterns in data to make predictions or decisions.

ML in Daily Life

  • Recommendations on Netflix and Amazon.
  • Image and speech recognition, such as Siri and Google Assistant.
  • Fraud detection by banks.
  • Self-driving cars.

options: A machine that works without electricity
The ability of a computer or machine to perform tasks that typically require human intelligence
A computer game played against the computer
A robot that looks exactly like a human

options: Storing files on a hard disk
mcqs.why: Understanding language and recognizing images are listed in the unit as tasks that require human intelligence, so a machine doing them is showing artificial intelligence.

mcqs.q: Machine Learning (ML) is a branch of which field?
mcqs.why: The solved answers state that Machine Learning is a branch of Artificial Intelligence that enables computers to learn from data and improve their performance on tasks.

mcqs.q: How do ML algorithms improve their performance?
options: By following only fixed instructions typed by the user
By copying answers from the internet
By analyzing patterns in data to make predictions or decisions
mcqs.why: Instead of following specific instructions, ML algorithms analyze patterns in data to make predictions or decisions, which is how they learn and improve without explicit programming.

options: Typing a letter in a word processor
Saving a photo in a folder

mcqs.why: This is the book's own fill-in-the-blank: in ML, algorithms analyze patterns in data to make predictions or decisions, exactly as the exercise answer gives.

mcqs.why: The solved answer names Siri and Google Assistant as examples of image and speech recognition in daily life that rely on machine learning.

mcqs.q: How do banks use Machine Learning?
mcqs.why: Fraud detection by banks is one of the daily-life uses of ML listed in the unit, because ML can spot unusual patterns in transactions.

mcqs.q: True or False: ML algorithms require explicit programming to improve their performance on tasks.
mcqs.why: The statement is false: ML enables computers to learn from data and improve performance without being explicitly programmed, which is the whole idea of machine learning.

mcqs.q: AI is used in which of the following areas?
options: Healthcare, finance, education, transportation and entertainment
mcqs.why: The unit states that AI is used in healthcare, finance, education, transportation and entertainment to enhance efficiency, accuracy and decision-making.

lessons.title: 5G Technology and the Internet of Things
lessons.notes_html:
5G stands for the fifth generation of wireless technology. It is the latest improvement in mobile networks, offering much faster speeds, lower latency (delay) and the ability to connect many devices at once.

Key Benefits of 5G over 4G

  • Faster internet — download or stream content far faster than with 4G.
  • Lower latency — it reacts almost instantly, which is great for video calls, online gaming and controlling robots remotely.
  • Many devices at once — connects many devices without slowing down, useful for smart cities and smart homes.

5G supports smart cities, self-driving cars and smoother Virtual Reality.

The Internet of Things (IoT)

The Internet of Things refers to a network of physical objects — devices, vehicles, appliances and sensors — embedded with technology to connect to the internet and collect and exchange data. This lets objects communicate with each other and with users, making them smart. Examples are smart homes, wearable health devices and sensors used in factories.

Smart Thermostat

A smart thermostat, like the Nest, is an IoT device that learns your heating and cooling preferences over time. You can control it remotely through an app, and it automatically adjusts the temperature based on whether you are home or away, saving energy and reducing utility bills.

mcqs.q: What does 5G stand for?
options: The fifth version of a mobile phone
The fifth generation of wireless technology
mcqs.why: The unit explains that 5G stands for the fifth generation of wireless technology, the latest improvement in mobile networks after earlier generations like 4G.

mcqs.q: 5G offers much faster speeds and lower ___.
mcqs.why: Latency means delay. The book's exercise answer is latency: 5G offers much faster speeds and lower latency, so it reacts almost instantly.

mcqs.q: Which is a key benefit of 5G over 4G?
options: It works without any signal towers
It removes the need for the internet
It can connect many devices at once without slowing down
mcqs.why: The unit lists three key benefits of 5G: faster internet, lower latency, and the ability to connect many devices at once without slowing down, which is useful for smart cities and smart homes.

mcqs.q: What does the Internet of Things (IoT) refer to?
options: A network of computers inside one office
A network of physical objects that connect to the internet and collect and exchange data
A single website with many pages
A cable that joins two computers
mcqs.why: IoT refers to physical objects such as devices, vehicles, appliances and sensors that are embedded with technology to connect to the internet and collect and exchange data.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an IoT example from the unit?
options: A smart thermostat like the Nest
mcqs.why: The Nest smart thermostat is the unit's IoT example: it learns heating and cooling preferences over time and automatically adjusts the temperature.

mcqs.q: A smart thermostat can learn your preferences and automatically adjust the ___.
mcqs.why: This is the book's fill-in-the-blank answer: a smart thermostat like the Nest learns your heating and cooling preferences and automatically adjusts the temperature.

mcqs.q: How does a smart thermostat save energy?
options: It adjusts the temperature based on whether you are home or away
It turns off the whole house's electricity
mcqs.why: The solved answer explains that the Nest adjusts temperature based on whether you are home or away, which saves energy and reduces utility bills.

mcqs.q: Which technologies does 5G support, according to the unit?
options: Smart cities, self-driving cars and smoother Virtual Reality
mcqs.why: With 5G we can download or stream content far faster than with 4G, and it supports smart cities, self-driving cars and smoother Virtual Reality.

mcqs.q: True or False: 5G technology allows for slower internet speeds compared to 4G technology.
mcqs.why: The statement is false. 5G is the latest improvement in mobile networks and offers much faster speeds than 4G, not slower ones.

mcqs.q: Which of these are physical objects that can be part of the IoT?
mcqs.why: The unit's IoT definition names devices, vehicles, appliances and sensors as the physical objects embedded with technology to connect to the internet and exchange data.

lessons.title: Robotics and Virtual Reality
lessons.notes_html:
Robotics is the field of technology that focuses on designing, building and using robots — machines capable of carrying out tasks automatically. Robots can be programmed to perform tasks either independently or with some degree of human input, often mimicking human actions or improving upon them.

Main Features of Robots

  • Sensors — let the robot perceive its environment.
  • Actuators — move the robot's parts.
  • Artificial Intelligence (AI), programmability and autonomy.

Robots in Industry

In warehouses, Amazon's warehouse robots transport products and speed up order processing. In car manufacturing, robotic arms in factories like Toyota and Tesla weld, paint and assemble car parts with precision and speed. Advantages: robots can work 24/7, handle repetitive tasks that would be tiring or dangerous for humans, carry heavy loads, and reduce human error while speeding up production.

Virtual Reality (VR)

Virtual Reality is a technology that creates a simulated environment, allowing users to experience and interact with a 3D world that is not real. By wearing a special VR headset, users are immersed in this digital environment, which feels lifelike because it surrounds their senses, primarily sight and sound. VR is used in gaming, for example the Oculus Quest, and in education through virtual classrooms and labs.

mcqs.q: What is robotics?
options: The field of technology that focuses on designing, building and using robots
mcqs.why: Robotics focuses on designing, building and using robots — machines capable of carrying out tasks automatically, either independently or with some human input.

mcqs.q: Robotics uses machines capable of carrying out tasks automatically, often with the help of ___.
mcqs.why: The unit lists sensors first among a robot's features, since sensors let the robot perceive its environment and act on it; the book's exercise answer is sensors.

options: Sensors, actuators, AI, programmability and autonomy
mcqs.why: The solved answer lists the main features of robots as sensors, actuators, Artificial Intelligence (AI), programmability and autonomy.

mcqs.q: What do sensors do for a robot?
options: Let the robot perceive its environment
Connect the robot to a printer
mcqs.why: Sensors let the robot perceive its environment so it can act on what it detects; actuators then move the robot's parts to carry out the task.

options: Amazon's warehouse robots transport products and speed up order processing
They guard the building at night
mcqs.why: The unit gives Amazon's warehouse robots as the example: they transport products and speed up order processing in warehouses.

mcqs.q: In car factories like Toyota and Tesla, robotic arms are used to ___.
options: weld, paint and assemble car parts
mcqs.why: The solved answer states that robotic arms in factories like Toyota and Tesla weld, paint and assemble car parts with precision and speed.

mcqs.q: Which is an advantage of using robots for automation?
options: They replace all human workers in every job
They can work 24/7 and handle repetitive or dangerous tasks
mcqs.why: Robots can work 24/7, handle repetitive tasks that would be tiring or dangerous for humans, carry heavy loads, and reduce human error while speeding up production.

mcqs.q: What is Virtual Reality (VR)?
options: A technology that creates a simulated environment users can experience and interact with
A real place visited by tourists
mcqs.why: VR creates a simulated environment, allowing users to experience and interact with a 3D world that is not real, through a special headset.

mcqs.q: Users wear a special headset in VR, which creates a simulated ___.
mcqs.why: The book's exercise answer is environment: VR creates a simulated environment that surrounds the user's senses, primarily sight and sound.

mcqs.q: Which is an example of VR in use?
options: The Oculus Quest in gaming, and virtual classrooms and labs in education
mcqs.why: The unit names the Oculus Quest for gaming and virtual classrooms and labs for education as the uses of Virtual Reality.

lessons.title: Holographic Imaging, CAT Tools and Blockchain
lessons.notes_html:
Holographic imaging creates images that appear 3D and can be viewed without special glasses.

Computer-Assisted Translation (CAT)

Computer-Assisted Translation refers to the use of software tools to help translators produce accurate and consistent translations more efficiently. CAT tools support human translators with features like translation memory, terminology databases and text segmentation. They store previously translated segments so they can be reused. A popular CAT tool used by professional translators and companies is SDL Trados.

Blockchain Technology

Blockchain is a digital system for recording transactions that ensures they are secure and transparent. Once recorded, transactions cannot be changed retroactively. Blockchain is used in cryptocurrencies, supply chain management and smart contracts.

Emerging Technologies

AI, 5G and Blockchain are three examples of emerging technologies: AI improves efficiency and decision-making in healthcare, finance and education; 5G gives faster speeds and lower latency; Blockchain records transactions securely and transparently.

mcqs.why: The book's exercise answer is glasses: holographic imaging creates images that appear 3D and can be viewed without special glasses.

mcqs.why: The unit's answer on emerging technologies states that blockchain records transactions securely and transparently and is used in cryptocurrencies, supply chain management and smart contracts.

mcqs.why: The solved answer lists AI, 5G technology and Blockchain technology as three examples of emerging technologies and explains the significance of each one.

chapters.title: Unit 2: Data Communication and Computer Networks

lessons.title: Data Communication and Types of Networks
lessons.notes_html:
Data communication is the process of sending and receiving data, like messages or information, between two or more devices. These devices could be computers, smartphones or even gaming consoles. For communication to happen, devices need to be connected in some way, which is where networks come in.

The Data Communication Process

Data travels in this order: Source device → Transmission medium → Destination device.

Types of Networks

  • Local Area Network (LAN) — connects devices over a small geographical area, like a home or office.
  • Wide Area Network (WAN) — covers a large geographical area, often globally, connecting devices that are located far apart.

Virtual Private Network (VPN)

A VPN is not a physical network but a secure, encrypted connection created over another network, like the internet. Its purpose is to protect data, especially when connecting to public networks; businesses use VPNs to allow employees to access company resources remotely and safely.

mcqs.q: What is data communication?
options: A way of storing data on a disk
The process of sending and receiving data between two or more devices
The process of charging a device
mcqs.why: Data communication is the process of sending and receiving data, like messages or information, between two or more devices such as computers, smartphones or gaming consoles.

mcqs.q: What is the correct order of the data communication process?
options: Source device → Transmission medium → Destination device
Destination device → Transmission medium → Source device
Transmission medium → Destination device → Source device
Source device → Destination device → Transmission medium
mcqs.why: Data starts at the source device, travels through the transmission medium, and arrives at the destination device — this is the book's own MCQ answer.

mcqs.q: Which of the following best describes a Wide Area Network (WAN)?
options: A network that covers a small geographical area like a home or office
A network that connects computers within one building only
A network that covers a large geographical area, often globally
A network used by one person on one computer
mcqs.why: A WAN is designed to connect devices that are located far apart, even globally, unlike a LAN which covers a small area like a home or office.

mcqs.q: True or False: A Local Area Network (LAN) can connect devices over a large geographic area like a city.
mcqs.why: The statement is false: a LAN connects devices over a small geographical area like a home or office; networks covering cities or the globe are WANs.

mcqs.q: Which devices can take part in data communication?
mcqs.why: The unit states that the devices in data communication could be computers, smartphones, or even gaming consoles, as long as they are connected in some way.

mcqs.q: What is the purpose of a Virtual Private Network (VPN)?
options: To store files in the cloud
To connect a printer to a computer
To create a secure, encrypted connection that protects data over another network
mcqs.why: A VPN is a secure, encrypted connection created over another network like the internet; its purpose is to protect data, especially on public networks.

mcqs.q: Businesses use VPNs so that employees can ___.
options: access company resources remotely and safely
mcqs.why: The solved answer explains that businesses use VPNs to allow employees to access company resources remotely and safely.

mcqs.q: A home network that connects your computer to the internet through a router is an example of a ___.
mcqs.why: The unit's router answer gives this example: a router connects your home network (LAN) to the internet (WAN), deciding the best path for data to travel.

mcqs.q: For data communication to happen, devices need to be ___.
options: kept in the same room always
connected in some way, which is where networks come in
mcqs.why: The unit states that for communication to happen, devices need to be connected in some way, which is where networks come in.

mcqs.q: True or False: A WAN is designed to connect devices that are located far apart, even globally.
mcqs.why: The statement is true: a Wide Area Network connects devices located far apart, often spanning countries or the whole globe.

lessons.title: Core Networking Components: Router, Modem and Switch
lessons.notes_html:
Networks are built from core components such as routers, modems and switches. A keyboard is an input device — it is not a networking component.

Router

A router is a device that connects different networks and sends data between them; it can connect your home network (LAN) to the internet (WAN). Its role is to decide the best path for data to travel to reach its destination. The router is the device primarily responsible for sending data between different networks.

Modem

The main function of a modem is to convert digital signals to analog and vice versa, so computer data can travel over lines such as telephone networks.

Switch and Hub

A switch connects devices within a network and forwards data to the right device. A hub is a simpler connecting device. Neither of them replaces the router's job of joining different networks together.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT a core networking component?
mcqs.why: A keyboard is an input device, not a networking component. Routers, modems and switches are the core networking components named in the book's MCQ.

mcqs.q: What is the role of a router in a network?
options: It converts digital signals to analog
It amplifies the signal strength only
It connects different networks and decides the best path for data to reach its destination
mcqs.why: A router connects different networks and sends data between them; its role is to decide the best path for data to travel to reach its destination.

mcqs.q: Which device is primarily responsible for sending data between different networks?
mcqs.why: The router is the device that connects multiple networks and routes data between them, which is why it is responsible for sending data between different networks.

mcqs.q: What is the main function of a modem in a network?
options: To amplify the signal strength of the network
To convert digital signals to analog and vice versa
To manage network security and data encryption
mcqs.why: A modem converts digital signals to analog and vice versa, so that computer data can travel over communication lines such as telephone networks.

mcqs.q: True or False: A router is a device that connects multiple networks and routes data between them.
mcqs.why: The statement is true: connecting multiple networks and routing data between them is exactly the router's job, for example joining a home LAN to the internet WAN.

mcqs.q: A router can connect your home network (LAN) to which larger network?
mcqs.why: The unit's example: a router can connect your home network (LAN) to the internet (WAN) and decides the best path for data to travel.

mcqs.q: Which device converts signals so data can travel over telephone networks?
mcqs.why: Converting digital signals to analog and vice versa is the modem's function, which is what allows data to travel over telephone lines.

mcqs.q: What type of cable is commonly used for telephone networks?
mcqs.why: The book's MCQ answer is twisted pair cable, the cable type commonly used for telephone networks; fiber optic and coaxial cables serve other purposes.

mcqs.q: Deciding the best path for data to travel is the job of the ___.
mcqs.why: The solved short answer states that the router's role is to decide the best path for data to travel to reach its destination.

mcqs.q: Which of these connects devices within the same network and forwards data to the right device?
mcqs.why: A switch connects devices within a network and forwards data to the correct device, while the router joins different networks together.

lessons.title: Guided Media: Twisted Pair, Coaxial and Fiber Optic Cables
lessons.notes_html:
Transmission media refers to the pathway through which data or information is sent from one device to another. It can be physical (Guided), like cables, or wireless (Unguided), like radio waves.

Guided Media

Guided media are physical cables — twisted pair, coaxial, fiber optic and USB cables — which guide the data along a specific path, directed to a specific device. Twisted pair cable is commonly used for telephone networks.

Fiber Optic Cable

A fiber optic cable is a cable made of glass that sends data as flashes of light; it is used to make the internet super fast. It differs from copper cables (twisted pair and coaxial), which carry data as electrical signals, are slower, suffer more interference and lose signal over long distances.

Fiber Optic vs Copper

  • Advantages of fiber: super fast; sends data far without losing quality; carries lots of data; no interference from other signals; thin and light, so easy to handle.
  • Disadvantages of fiber: costly; delicate — bending too much can break it; special equipment and skilled people are needed to install and fix it; not available everywhere yet.
  • Copper cables are affordable and flexible, but have limited speed, crosstalk issues, and the signal weakens over longer cables.

The coaxial cable's labelled parts are: outside insulation, insulation, copper mesh and copper wire.

mcqs.q: What does transmission media refer to?
options: The pathway through which data is sent from one device to another
The software used to write emails
mcqs.why: Transmission media refers to the pathway through which data or information is sent from one device to another; it can be physical (guided) like cables or wireless (unguided) like radio waves.

mcqs.q: Which type of transmission medium uses light to transmit data over long distances?
mcqs.why: A fiber optic cable is made of glass and sends data as flashes of light, which lets it carry lots of data over far places without losing quality.

mcqs.q: Guided transmission media are ___.
options: physical cables that guide data along a specific path
mcqs.why: Guided media are physical cables, like twisted pair, coaxial, fiber optic and USB cables, which guide the data along a specific path to a specific device.

mcqs.q: How do copper cables like twisted pair and coaxial carry data?
mcqs.why: Copper cables carry data as electrical signals; they are slower than fiber, suffer more interference and lose signal over long distances.

mcqs.q: Which is an advantage of fiber optic cables compared to copper cables?
options: They carry lots of data over far places without losing quality and have no interference
They can be bent sharply without damage
Anyone can fix them without training
mcqs.why: Fiber optic advantages from the unit: super fast, sends data far without losing quality, carries lots of data, no interference from other signals, and thin and light so easy to handle.

mcqs.q: Which is a disadvantage of fiber optic cables?
options: They are costly and delicate, and bending them too much can break them
They lose signal quickly over distance
mcqs.why: The unit lists fiber's disadvantages: costly; delicate, so bending too much can break them; special equipment needed; fixing is tricky and needs skilled people; not available everywhere yet.

mcqs.q: True or False: Fiber optic cables are known for their ability to transmit data at slow speeds.
mcqs.why: The statement is false: fiber optic cables are used to make the internet super fast, carrying data as flashes of light over long distances.

options: Outside insulation, insulation, copper mesh and copper wire
Glass core and plastic coating only
mcqs.why: The unit's labelled diagram on page 21 is for the coaxial cable: outside insulation, insulation, copper mesh and copper wire.

mcqs.q: Copper cables are affordable and flexible, but they have ___.
options: the highest speed of all media
limited speed, crosstalk issues, and signal weakening over longer cables
mcqs.why: The comparison in the unit states that copper cables are affordable and flexible but have limited speed, crosstalk issues, and the signal weakens over longer cables.

mcqs.q: Why is fiber optic cable not bothered by other signals?
options: It carries data as light inside glass instead of electrical signals in copper
mcqs.why: Because fiber sends data as flashes of light through glass, it has no interference from other signals, unlike copper cables carrying electrical signals.

lessons.title: Unguided Media: Radio Waves, Microwaves, Infrared and Satellite
lessons.notes_html:
Unguided media are the wireless transmission of data through the air or space using electromagnetic waves. They have no defined physical pathway and often broadcast signals so that more than one device in range can receive the data.

Types of Unguided Media

  • Radio waves — used by Wi-Fi networks in homes and public places.
  • Microwaves — high-frequency waves used for long-distance links between towers.
  • Infrared — short-range communication; it cannot pass through walls and obstacles.
  • Satellite communication — wireless, so it is unguided media even though it covers huge distances.

Microwave Communication

Microwave communication requires a clear line of sight between the transmitter and receiver, because microwaves are high-frequency waves that cannot pass through buildings easily. Microwave towers send signals between each other to cover large distances.

Advantages and Disadvantages

The major advantage of unguided media is mobility and wireless connectivity — no cables are needed. A common application is Wi-Fi networks in homes and public places. The trade-off is that wireless signals can suffer interference and are less secure than guided media.

mcqs.q: Unguided media refers to which type of communication?
options: Communication over the Internet using fiber optics
mcqs.why: Unguided media transmit data wirelessly through the air or space using electromagnetic waves, with no defined physical pathway — this is the book's MCQ answer.

mcqs.q: What do unguided media use for data transmission?
options: Electromagnetic waves such as radio waves, microwaves, infrared and satellite signals
mcqs.why: The solved short answer states that unguided media use electromagnetic waves — radio waves, microwaves, infrared and satellite communication — without any defined physical pathway.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a major advantage of using unguided media?
options: Long-distance communication without any signal loss
mcqs.why: The book's MCQ answer is mobility and wireless connectivity: unguided media need no cables, so devices can move freely while staying connected.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a common application of unguided media?
options: Wi-Fi networks in homes and public places
Fiber optic cables for Internet service providers
mcqs.why: Wi-Fi networks in homes and public places use radio waves, a form of unguided media; the other options all use physical cables, which are guided media.

mcqs.q: What is required for microwave communication?
options: A cable between the two towers
A clear line of sight between the transmitter and receiver
mcqs.why: Microwaves are high-frequency waves that cannot pass through buildings easily, so microwave communication requires a clear line of sight between transmitter and receiver.

mcqs.q: True or False: Infrared communication can transmit data through walls and obstacles.
mcqs.why: The statement is false: infrared cannot pass through walls and obstacles, which is why it is only used for short-range communication in the same room.

mcqs.q: True or False: Satellite communication is classified as guided media since it requires physical cables.
mcqs.why: The statement is false: satellite communication is wireless transmission through space, so it belongs to unguided media, not guided media.

mcqs.q: True or False: Wi-Fi networks are a form of unguided media that use radio waves for wireless communication.
mcqs.why: The statement is true: Wi-Fi is listed in the unit as a common application of unguided media, using radio waves for wireless communication.

mcqs.q: How do microwave towers cover large distances?
options: They send signals between each other from tower to tower
They bounce signals off the moon
They store data and carry it physically
mcqs.why: The unit explains that microwave towers send signals between each other to cover large distances, each link keeping a clear line of sight.

mcqs.q: True or False: The main disadvantage of unguided media is that it is less mobile compared to guided media.
mcqs.why: The statement is false — it is the opposite: mobility is the main advantage of unguided media, since no cables tie the devices down.

lessons.title: Spreadsheets: Worksheets, Workbooks and Cells
lessons.notes_html:
A spreadsheet is primarily used for organizing and working with data. In programs like Microsoft Excel, data is typed into tables made of rows and columns.

Rows, Columns and Cells

  • Rows — the horizontal lines used for organizing data.
  • Columns — the vertical lines used for categorizing data.
  • Grid — the pattern formed by the intersecting rows and columns.
  • Cell — the smallest unit within the grid, where a row and a column meet; it is the basic unit where data is stored, and every cell has a unique name called the cell address.

Worksheet and Workbook

A worksheet is the single work area where we type data in the form of tables. In Excel 2016, a worksheet has 1,048,576 rows (numbered 1 to 1,048,576) and 16,384 columns (labeled A to XFD). A workbook is the collection of worksheets: all the worksheets are saved in one workbook as one file, and we can work in more than one worksheet at a time.

Active and Passive Cells

The selected cell is called the active cell; a bold rectangle indicates it, and we enter data by typing on the keyboard. Cells that are not currently selected are passive cells and cannot be edited until made active. The Quick Access Toolbar can be customized for quick access to common commands and functions.

mcqs.q: What is a spreadsheet primarily used for?
mcqs.why: The book's MCQ answer: a spreadsheet is primarily used for organizing and working with data in rows and columns, as in Excel and Google Sheets.

mcqs.q: What do we call the horizontal lines used for organizing data in a spreadsheet?
mcqs.why: Rows are the horizontal lines of a spreadsheet, numbered 1, 2, 3 and so on; columns are the vertical lines, labeled with letters.

mcqs.q: What do we call the vertical lines used for categorizing data in a spreadsheet?
mcqs.why: Columns are the vertical lines, labeled A, B, C up to XFD in Excel 2016; rows run horizontally across the sheet.

mcqs.q: What does the grid in Excel refer to?
mcqs.why: The grid is the pattern formed by the intersecting rows and columns of the worksheet; each square in the grid is called a cell.

mcqs.q: What is the smallest unit within an Excel grid used to input and store data?

lessons.title: Computational Thinking and Problem Solving
lessons.notes_html:
Computational thinking is a method of solving problems using techniques and skills that are common in computer science. It is not just limited to computers; it also helps us solve everyday problems efficiently. Its four key concepts are decomposition, pattern recognition, abstraction and algorithm design.

Problem Solving

Problem-solving involves finding solutions to issues or difficulties. A problem is a situation, task or question that needs to be solved or dealt with. The problem-solving strategies in this unit are:

  • Identify the problem clearly.
  • Break the problem down (decomposition).
  • Look for patterns.
  • Develop an algorithm.
  • Test and improve the solution.

A problem-solving approach is important because it turns a large, complex problem into smaller parts that can be solved individually, making the whole problem easier to manage.

Logic

In problem-solving, logic means using reasoning and rationality to arrive at conclusions. Conditions in a program are logical statements or expressions that evaluate to either true or false, using comparison operators (==, >, <) and logical operators (AND, OR, NOT).

lessons.title: Algorithms: Characteristics and How to Write Them
lessons.notes_html:
An algorithm is a step-by-step set of instructions designed to solve a specific problem or complete a task, like a recipe for cooking that tells you exactly what to do, step by step, to get a result. The word algorithm is named after the famous mathematician Muhammad Ibne Musa Al-Khwarizmi.

Characteristics of an Algorithm

  • Input — an algorithm may or may not require input.
  • Output — each algorithm is expected to produce at least one result.
  • Definiteness — each instruction must be clear and unambiguous.
  • Finiteness — it should terminate after a finite number of steps; finite time means a limited and defined period of time.

How to Write an Algorithm

  • Understand the problem and identify the input and the output.
  • Plan the steps (decomposition).
  • Write the algorithm in simple language using commands like Start, Input, Add and Display.
  • Ensure the algorithm is complete.
  • Test the algorithm.

Rules for writing algorithms: clear problem statement, step-by-step instructions, specific and clear steps, good names, logical order, and be brief. Advantages: an algorithm is a stepwise representation of a solution, which makes it easy to understand; it uses a definite procedure; it is not dependent on any programming language; and every step has its own logical sequence, so it is easy to debug.

Design

In problem-solving, design means creating the step-by-step plan of the solution — algorithm design. Once the problem is broken down, we create a clear plan of action that can be followed, and then test and improve the solution.

lessons.title: Flowcharts and Their Symbols
lessons.notes_html:
A flowchart is the diagrammatic/graphical representation of the sequence of steps to solve a problem; it is also known as a blueprint of a design used for solving a specific problem. The first design of flowchart was designed by John Von Neumann in 1945. Its purpose is to communicate the logic of a program clearly.

Standard Flowchart Symbols

SymbolUsed For
OvalStart and End of flowchart
ParallelogramInput and Output operations
RectangleProcessing — arithmetic operations and data manipulations
DiamondDecision making, with two/three alternatives such as true and false
ArrowsFlow lines that indicate the flow of logic
CircleSame page connector
LinkOff page connector

Advantages and Rules

Advantages: a flowchart is an excellent way of communicating the logic of a program; it is easy and efficient to analyze a problem; it acts as a blueprint, making program development easier; it makes maintenance easier; and it is easy to convert into any programming language code. Rules for drawing: use the standard shapes, begin and end with ovals labeled Start and End, give each shape one arrow in and one arrow out, label shapes simply, use diamonds for decisions with Yes/No labels, and keep connections clean.

Computer Programs

A computer program is a set of instructions for a computer to follow. The Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) is the classic problem of finding the shortest route to visit cities and return to the starting city.

lessons.title: Algorithms in Action: Swapping, Minimum and Even or Odd
lessons.notes_html:
The unit's class activities turn everyday problems into algorithms and flowcharts.

Swap Two Numbers Using a Temporary Variable

Algorithm: Step-1 Start. Step-2 Input two numbers, say A, B. Step-3 TEMP = A. Step-4 A = B. Step-5 B = TEMP. Step-6 Display the values of A, B after the swap. Step-7 Stop. In the flowchart, a parallelogram takes the input, rectangles do TEMP = A, A = B and B = TEMP, and a parallelogram prints A, B.

Compare Two Numbers to Find the Minimum

Algorithm: 1. Start. 2. Read the first number A. 3. Read the second number B. 4. If A is less than B, print “A is the minimum number”. 5. Else print “B is the minimum number”. 6. End. The decision is drawn as a diamond: Is A < B?

Check Whether a Number Is Even or Odd

Algorithm: 1. Start. 2. Read the value of N. 3. If N is divisible by 2 (N % 2 equals 0), print “N is Even”. 4. Else print “N is Odd”. 5. End. The diamond asks: Is N % 2 = 0?

mcqs.q: In the swap algorithm, why is a temporary variable TEMP used?
options: To hold the value of A safely while A is overwritten with B's value
To store the final answer forever
mcqs.why: TEMP = A keeps the original value of A safe; after A = B, the step B = TEMP puts the saved value into B, completing the swap without losing data.

mcqs.q: What are the three middle steps of the swap algorithm, in order?
options: TEMP = A, then A = B, then B = TEMP
A = B, then B = A, then TEMP = A
TEMP = B, then B = TEMP, then A = TEMP
A = TEMP, then TEMP = B, then B = A
mcqs.why: The book's worked example: Step-3 TEMP = A, Step-4 A = B, Step-5 B = TEMP, then display the swapped values and stop.

mcqs.q: If A = 5 and B = 9 at the start, what are A and B after the swap algorithm runs?
mcqs.why: TEMP takes 5, A becomes 9, and B becomes TEMP's 5 — so the values are exchanged: A = 9 and B = 5.

options: Is A the same as TEMP?
mcqs.why: The flowchart uses a diamond 'Is A < B?' — on Yes it prints A is minimum; on No it prints B is minimum; both paths join to END.

mcqs.q: If A = 12 and B = 7 in the minimum algorithm, what is printed?
mcqs.why: A (12) is not less than B (7), so the Else path runs and the algorithm prints that B is the minimum number.

mcqs.q: In the even/odd algorithm, what does N % 2 = 0 test?
options: Whether N is a prime number
Whether N is divisible by 2 with no remainder
mcqs.why: The book's worked example: if N is divisible by 2 (N % 2 equals 0), print N is Even; else print N is Odd.

mcqs.q: Using the even/odd algorithm, the number 14 gives which output?
mcqs.why: 14 divided by 2 leaves no remainder (14 % 2 = 0), so the Yes path of the diamond prints that N is Even.

mcqs.q: Using the even/odd algorithm, the number 27 gives which output?
mcqs.why: 27 % 2 equals 1, not 0, so the Else path runs and the algorithm prints that N is Odd.

mcqs.why: Input and printing steps use parallelograms (Input Value of A, B; Print A, B), while decisions use diamonds and processing steps use rectangles.

mcqs.why: Rectangles represent processing — arithmetic operations and data manipulations such as TEMP = A, A = B and B = TEMP in the swap flowchart.

lessons.title: Loops in Algorithms: Tables and Sums
lessons.notes_html:
A loop repeats steps while a condition is true. In a flowchart, an arrow loops back to the decision diamond until the condition becomes false.

Print the Table of 7

Algorithm: 1. Start. 2. Set a variable i to 1. 3. Repeat while i <= 10: print 7 x i = 7*i; increment i by 1 (i = i + 1). 4. Stop. This prints 7 x 1 = 7, 7 x 2 = 14, and so on up to 7 x 10 = 70. The diamond asks: Is i <= 10? — on Yes, print and loop back; on No, go to END.

Print the First 10 Natural Numbers and Their Sum

Algorithm: 1. Start. 2. Set Sum = 0 and i = 1. 3. Repeat while i <= 10: print i; add i to Sum (Sum = Sum + i); increment i by 1. 4. Print Sum. 5. Stop. The numbers printed are 1 to 10 and their sum is 55.

mcqs.why: The algorithm repeats the steps while i <= 10: print 7 x i, then increment i by 1; when i passes 10 the loop stops.

mcqs.q: What is the last line printed by the table-of-7 algorithm?
mcqs.why: The loop runs for i = 1 to 10, so the last line printed is 7 x 10 = 70; the book's answer confirms the table runs up to 7 x 10 = 70.

mcqs.q: Why must i be incremented by 1 inside the loop?
options: So that i eventually passes 10 and the loop terminates
To print the same line again
mcqs.why: Incrementing i (i = i + 1) moves the loop forward each time; without it, i would stay at 1 forever and the loop would never end — an algorithm must finish in finite time.

mcqs.q: In the sum algorithm, what are the starting values?
mcqs.why: The algorithm starts with Sum = 0 and a variable i set to 1, then adds each value of i to Sum as the loop runs from 1 to 10.

mcqs.q: What is the sum of the first 10 natural numbers, as printed by the algorithm?
mcqs.why: Adding 1 + 2 + ... + 10 gives 55; the book's answer confirms the numbers printed are 1 to 10 and their sum is 55.

mcqs.q: In the sum flowchart, where does the arrow go when the diamond's answer is Yes?
options: It loops back through the print and add steps to the diamond again
mcqs.why: On Yes (i <= 10), the flowchart prints i, adds i to Sum, increments i, and an arrow loops back to the diamond; on No it prints Sum and ends.

mcqs.q: When does the sum algorithm print the final Sum?
options: After the loop finishes, when i has passed 10
mcqs.why: The Print Sum step comes after the loop: the flowchart's No path from the diamond leads to Print Sum and then END.

mcqs.q: In the table-of-7 flowchart, which step is drawn as a rectangle?
mcqs.why: Processing steps such as i = i + 1 are rectangles; the decision is a diamond, input/output are parallelograms, and Start/End are ovals.

mcqs.q: A loop in an algorithm is an example of which idea from this unit?
options: Repeating steps under a condition until the condition becomes false
mcqs.why: Both worked examples repeat steps while a condition (i <= 10) is true, and stop when it becomes false — that is how loops work in algorithms and flowcharts.

mcqs.q: If the condition in the table-of-7 loop were i <= 5 instead, how many lines would print?
options: 5 lines, from 7 x 1 up to 7 x 5
mcqs.why: The loop prints one line per value of i; with i running from 1 to 5 it would print 5 lines, ending at 7 x 5 = 35.

lessons.title: Scratch and Block-Based Programming
lessons.notes_html:
Scratch is a tool developed by MIT Media Lab (USA) in 2003. It is used to make stories through animations and visual effects, and the developed stories, scripts, animations and games can be shared online. This programming language is called the educational programming language; it is mainly for children (ages 8–16) and is free.

Block-Based Programming

Scratch uses visual coding: programming by snapping together picture blocks instead of typing text commands. Blocks are the units in Scratch programming. Each block has its own set of functions and properties and is unique from the others. Multiple blocks joined together become a program that works as a single unit.

Scripts

You click on the Scripts tab to write a script. Scripts are built in the Scripts Area by dragging blocks from the Blocks Area and snapping them together; a script is the name of a program or method — it tells the actor (sprite) what to do. A Scratch project encompasses various works like games, stories, animations or artworks created using code.

lessons.title: Block Categories: Motion, Looks, Sound, Sensing and More
lessons.notes_html:
Scratch provides over 100 code blocks, organized into eight categories on the blocks palette: Motion, Looks, Sound, Pen, Control, Sensing, Numbers (Operators) and Variables.

What the Categories Control

  • Motion — moves sprites, for example the MOVE block (move 10 steps).
  • Looks — controls the appearance of sprites and text.
  • Sound — controls playback and volume of audio.
  • Sensing — determines the location of the mouse-pointer, its distance from other sprites, and whether a sprite is touching another sprite. The touching block is in the Sensing category.
  • Numbers (Operators) — works with numbers and conditions such as Boolean expressions.

Adding Sound to a Script

Steps: (1) Select Sound. (2) Select the Play drum block. (3) Drag out a PLAY DRUM block and snap it onto the MOVE block, for example: move 10 steps; play drum 15 for 0.25 beats. (4) Click and listen. (5) Choose different drums from the pull-down menu: Snare Drum, Bass Drum, Side Stick, Crash Cymbal and Open Hi-Hat.

Boolean Expressions

A Boolean Expression is a true or false question — it gives one of two answers, true or false, and is used in conditions.

lessons.title: Control Blocks: Forever, If-Then and Cloning
lessons.notes_html:
The Control category holds the blocks that decide how scripts run: repeating, choosing and duplicating.

Forever Block

The Forever block is used for creating infinite patterns — it repeats the blocks inside it again and again, without stopping.

If-Then Block

The if() then block executes a set of code if a condition is true, similar to if-else statements in other languages. The condition is only checked once — which is why the forever block is often wrapped around it. In the unit's puzzle, the stack forever → if mouse down? → say Hello! for 2 secs works like this: the forever block keeps the check running again and again; whenever the mouse button is pressed, the sprite says Hello! for 2 seconds. Without forever, the script would test the mouse only a single time at the start and then finish.

Iteration

Iteration means repeating actions or tasks — the forever block is Scratch's way of iterating forever.

Cloning

Cloning is used to duplicate a sprite with shared behavior — making copies of a sprite that behave the same way.

lessons.title: Digital Citizenship and Its Key Elements
lessons.notes_html:
Digital citizenship refers to the responsible and appropriate use of technology and the internet. It involves understanding how to use digital tools, such as smartphones, computers and the internet, in a safe, respectful and ethical manner. Being a good digital citizen means knowing your rights and responsibilities online, and behaving in ways that protect yourself and others.

The Seven Key Elements

  • Online Safety — protecting personal information and understanding how to avoid online dangers such as scams or cyberbullying.
  • Digital Etiquette — communicating respectfully and responsibly with others online, using good manners in emails, social media and messaging platforms. (Etiquette does not mean inappropriate language and behavior online.)
  • Digital Literacy — knowing how to use technology effectively and evaluate the credibility of online sources.
  • Privacy and Security — including creating strong passwords.
  • Cyberbullying Awareness.
  • Intellectual Property — giving credit to original creators of content.
  • Digital Footprint.

Why Digital Literacy Matters

Digital literacy means knowing how to use technology effectively and evaluate the credibility of online sources. It is important because a digital citizen must be able to judge which online information can be trusted, instead of believing or spreading misinformation.

lessons.title: Privacy, Security and Email Safety
lessons.notes_html:
Privacy and security are important elements of digital citizenship, including creating strong passwords.

Email Privacy and Security

A key practice for maintaining email privacy and security is using strong passwords. To maintain privacy, avoid sharing sensitive information through email, such as passwords, financial data or personal identification numbers. Also be wary of phishing emails from unknown senders that request personal information or contain suspicious links.

Protecting Your Accounts from Cybercrime

  • Use strong passwords — a complex mix of letters, numbers and symbols; change them regularly and do not use the same password across multiple accounts.
  • Enable two-factor authentication (2FA) for an extra layer of security.
  • Keep software updated, including operating systems, applications and antivirus software.
  • Be wary of phishing attempts; verify the source of emails or messages before clicking links or downloading attachments.
  • Use secure connections and avoid public Wi-Fi for sensitive transactions; a VPN can help secure your internet connection, especially on public networks.
  • Regularly monitor accounts for suspicious activity; be cautious with personal information; report cyber crime; and back up important data.

Best Practice for Ethical Digital Use

A best practice for ethical digital use is to use strong passwords and enable two-factor authentication — and to think about the impact of your posts on others before posting.

lessons.title: Plagiarism, Copyright and Piracy
lessons.notes_html:
Plagiarism is the act of using someone else's work, ideas or expressions without proper acknowledgment, presenting them as your own. It is the unethical practice of using someone else's work or ideas without giving proper credit. Plagiarism is considered a serious offense in academic and professional settings; it not only disrespects the original creator's rights but also undermines the integrity of the educational and professional systems.

Copyright, Plagiarism and Piracy — the Difference

  • Copyright is a legal framework that grants creators exclusive rights to their original works — literature, music, art and software — allowing them to control how their creations are used and distributed. It deals with legal rights.
  • Plagiarism is the unethical practice of using someone else's work or ideas without giving proper credit, presenting them as one's own. It pertains to ethical behavior.
  • Piracy is the unauthorized use, reproduction or distribution of copyrighted materials, such as downloading or sharing movies and software without permission. It concerns unauthorized use of content.

Note the related wrong practice from the exercise: unauthorized copying of software is piracy, not plagiarism.

lessons.title: Cyberbullying and Cybercrime
lessons.notes_html:
Cyberbullying involves using digital platforms, such as social media, messaging apps or online forums, to harass, intimidate or embarrass someone. It can take many forms, including spreading rumors, sending threatening messages, sharing embarrassing photos, or impersonating someone online. Victims may experience emotional distress, anxiety, depression, and a decline in academic performance or social interactions, and it can have severe consequences.

Preventing Cyberbullying

  • Be mindful of what you share — limit personal information shared online to reduce the risk of becoming a target.
  • Adjust privacy settings on social media accounts to control who can see your posts and interact with you.
  • Think before you post — consider the potential impact of your comments or images before sharing them online.
  • Victims should document evidence, report it on the platform, and talk to someone they trust; bystanders should stand up against bullying and not engage with trolls.

Cybercrime

Cybercrime refers to criminal activities conducted through the internet or involving computer systems. It includes a wide range of offenses, from identity theft and hacking to online fraud and cyberbullying. Its types include identity theft, hacking, phishing, online fraud, cyberbullying and malware attacks (viruses, worms and ransomware). Identity theft is stealing personal information to impersonate someone else. Cyber trolls seek to provoke and upset people online — not to promote positive discussion.

lessons.title: Social Media: Advantages and Disadvantages
lessons.notes_html:
Social media connects users all over the world, but it must be used responsibly — it can be used for business and marketing as well as personal communication.

Advantages of Social Media

  • Connectivity — users connect with people from all over the world, fostering friendships and relationships.
  • Access to Information — news and information quickly and easily.
  • Creativity and Expression — a platform to express oneself through posts, photos and videos.
  • Business Opportunities — businesses reach a wider audience and market products at lower cost than traditional advertising.
  • Support and Community — users find support in groups that share similar interests.

Disadvantages of Social Media

  • Privacy Concerns — sharing personal information can lead to privacy issues and identity theft.
  • Cyberbullying — a platform for bullying and harassment with serious emotional impacts.
  • Misinformation — false information spreads quickly, leading to misunderstandings and panic.
  • Addiction — can affect mental health and productivity.
  • Decreased Face-to-Face Interaction — overreliance can decline real-life social interactions.

lessons.notes_html:
The main goal of entrepreneurship is to create jobs and make a profit. A business plan outlines a company's objectives, strategies and operational plans to achieve its goals, and serves as a roadmap for the business.

Types of Entrepreneurship

  • Small Business Entrepreneurship — primarily focuses on local businesses.
  • Scalable Startup Entrepreneurship — startups built to grow large.
  • Corporate Entrepreneurship — entrepreneurship inside a large company.
  • Intrapreneurship — employees act like entrepreneurs within their company.
  • Lifestyle Entrepreneurship and Social Entrepreneurship — other types named in the exercise.
  • Technological Entrepreneurship.

lessons.title: The Business Plan
lessons.notes_html:
A business plan is a detailed document that outlines the goals, strategies and operational plans of a business. Its primary purpose is to serve as a roadmap for starting and managing a business, helping entrepreneurs understand how to run their business effectively and attract investors or lenders.

Key Aspects (Components) of a Business Plan

  • Market Need — the problem the business aims to solve or the need it seeks to fulfill; it helps identify the problem your business aims to solve.
  • Product Design — the products or services offered, including features and benefits.
  • Costing — the costs of producing the product or delivering the service, which helps determine pricing and profitability.
  • Operations — how the business will run day-to-day, including processes, facilities and logistics.
  • Marketing — how the business will be promoted and customers attracted.

Value Proposition

A Value Proposition is a statement made by a company to customers, explaining why its offerings are the best choice for consumers.

lessons.title: Digital Marketing and Its Components
lessons.notes_html:
Digital marketing refers to the use of the internet and online-based technologies to promote products or services. It encompasses a variety of online marketing strategies aimed at reaching consumers through digital channels, and it includes various digital advertising methods and channels as part of a broader marketing strategy.

Key Components of Digital Marketing

  • Search Engine Optimization (SEO)
  • Content Marketing
  • Email Marketing — sending promotional messages via email.
  • Pay-Per-Click (PPC)
  • Social Media Marketing

Product Design is not a component of digital marketing — it is a component of the business plan.

The Digital Marketing Plan

A Digital Marketing Plan outlines the strategies and actions that a business will take to reach its target audience online. Its components are: Executive Summary (which outlines the main goals and actions), Target Audience, Marketing Goals and Objectives, Digital Marketing Channels, Content Strategy, Budget, Performance Metrics and KPIs, Timeline, Evaluation and Adjustment, and Conclusion. The plan is important because it helps businesses effectively promote their products and services through various digital channels.

lessons.title: SEO: Search Engine Optimization
lessons.notes_html:
SEO stands for Search Engine Optimization. It is a set of strategies and techniques used to improve the visibility of a website on search engines like Google.

The Main Goal of SEO

Its primary goal is to help websites get to the top positions in the search results so that more people can find them: when people search for information, products or services, they usually click on the websites that appear at the top of the search results.

How SEO Benefits a Website

  • More Visitors — if a website ranks higher in search results, it will attract more visitors, and this can lead to more sales or engagement.
  • Builds Trust — websites that appear at the top of search results are often viewed as more trustworthy and reliable by users, so a wider audience is willing to visit and use them.
  • Cost-Effective — unlike paid ads, which require ongoing payments, good SEO can bring in visitors for free over time, so the audience keeps growing without repeated advertising cost.

What SEO Optimizes

One aspect that SEO optimizes is the website's content: in the Digital Marketing Channels component, the unit defines SEO as optimizing website content to rank higher in search results. By improving the content so that it matches what people search for, the website's visibility increases and it appears nearer the top of the results. SEO does not aim to reduce a website's visibility, and it does not guarantee instant sales.
